Trail Session vs Color Cycle in Color Flip

Compare Color Flip’s two current modes: choose a swatch for each of ten targets, or rotate the active color after every submission.

By NoCharge·Reviewed by NoCharge·Published August 15, 2026·Updated November 24, 2026·2 min read
Try the detail in a live board.

Pick a color. Step carefully. Take your time.

Play Color FlipBrowse all Articles

Bottom line: Current Color Flip presents a ten-position target trail. Trail session lets you choose a color for each answer; Color cycle advances the active swatch after every submission.

Trail session: choose each answer

The next target is shown by name and swatch. Select Coral, Teal, Gold, or Violet, then lock the color to submit. Unless Rotate palette is enabled, the active swatch stays the same for the next position. You can also use Cycle color to advance it manually.

Color cycle: let the palette advance

Color cycle uses the same target trail and scoring, but the active swatch advances after each locked answer in the order Coral → Teal → Gold → Violet → Coral. You still read and submit one target at a time; there is no spatial board or turn-taking opponent.

Same ten-target objective

A match adds one to the score. A mismatch does not end the session, and both modes proceed through all ten submitted colors. A perfect ten is a win; any lower completed total is a draw. There is no timer, penalty for pausing, or stored best score.

Readable controls and current limits

The target names, palette labels, progress trail, and match total remain visible. The color buttons and mode controls are standard buttons; use Tab to focus them and Enter or Space to activate. The current build does not use arrow-key movement, Undo, per-mode local records, or My Arcade progress.

For the palette order and automatic rotation, read How Color Flip’s palette cycle works. The current game page has the live controls.
